lean.statement:
theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    let γ := ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E
    let f : E → E → ℝ := fun w x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ
    let df : E → E → E → ℝ := fun w v x => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ
    ∃ hf : ∀ w, MemLp (f w) 2 γ,
    ∃ hdf : ∀ w v, MemLp (df w v) 2 γ,
    ∃ D : E → E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 γ,
      (∀ w v, D w v = (hdf w v).toLp (df w v)) ∧
      ∀ w, HasFDerivAt (fun u => (hf u).toLp (f u)) (D w) w
approved_definition_context: stdGaussian E is the actual standard centered Gaussian measure on the displayed finite-dimensional real inner product space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure. Polynomial.eval, Polynomial.derivative and the real inner product have their usual literal meanings.

MemLp g 2 mu is genuine square integrability. Its toLp is the almost-everywhere equivalence class in the normed space Lp of real functions under the displayed measure. Different proofs of membership give the same class.

E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 mu denotes actual continuous real linear maps with the operator norm. HasFDerivAt F A w means that the norm of F(w+h)-F(w)-A(h), divided by the norm of h, tends to zero as the full ambient vector h tends to zero.
